rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying. Its only related links are for filing a complaint and the Young Worker Toolkit.

rules.name: Federal minimum age for most jobs (14)

rules.roles: Ages 14 and 15 may work in jobs the 14 and 15 year old rules allow, such as most retail, errands and delivery on foot, bicycle or public transit.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying. It only points to the Wage and Hour Division website and helpline.

rules.quote: Children under 14 years of age may not be employed

rules.name: Work hours for 14 and 15 year olds
rules.age_note: Applies to non-farm jobs outside school hours. Some states set tighter hours.
rules.roles: Jobs outside school hours: no more than 3 hours on a school day including Friday, no more than 18 hours in a school week, between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. (until 9 p.m. June 1 through Labor Day).
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying. It covers hours, permitted and prohibited work, and pay.
rules.quote: More than 3 hours on a school day, including Friday

rules.name: What jobs 14 and 15 year olds can and cannot do
rules.age_note: If a job is not specifically permitted for ages 14 and 15, it is prohibited.
rules.roles: Permitted: most retail (cashiering, selling, price marking, packing, shelving), errands or delivery on foot, bicycle or public transit, yard clean-up and grounds maintenance (no power mowers, cutters, or trimmers), hand car washing and polishing, simple food preparation and serving (limited cooking, no baking). Prohibited: baking, ladders and scaffolds, youth peddling, sign waving, door-to-door sales.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying.

rules.name: No door-to-door sales or sign waving at 14 and 15
rules.age_note: This ban applies to ages 14 and 15 in non-farm jobs. Check your state for more limits.
rules.roles: Not allowed at this age: youth peddling, sign waving, or door-to-door sales activities.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying.
rules.quote: youth peddling, sign waving, or door-to-door sales activities

rules.name: Jobs for 16 and 17 year olds
rules.age_note: Any job is allowed unless the Secretary of Labor declared it hazardous. No federal hour limit. States also have rules, and employers must follow both.
rules.roles: Any job that has not been declared hazardous, at unlimited hours.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying.
rules.quote: any job that has not been declared hazardous

rules.name: Jobs no one under 18 may do (hazardous list)
rules.age_note: The page sets an 18-year minimum age for these hazardous occupations. Apprentices and student-learners at least 16, in approved programs, get a limited exemption from some of these orders (power woodworking, metal forming, meat processing, bakery machines, balers, circular and chain saws, roofing, and trenching). The exemption does not cover the others.
rules.roles: Banned under 18 include: roofing, trenching and excavation (over 4 feet deep), logging and sawmilling, demolition, power-driven saws and woodworking machines, forklifts and cranes, on-road driving, coal and other mining, explosives, and meat-slicing and meat-packing machines.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying. It is a list of banned work.
rules.page_title: Fact Sheet #43: Child Labor Provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for Nonagricultural Occupations
rules.quote: establishes an 18-year minimum age for those nonagricultural occupations

rules.name: Babysitting, home chores, and paper routes
rules.age_note: The page says minor chores around private homes and casual babysitting are work the federal law does not cover. It lists delivering newspapers to customers as a permitted job for children under 14. Check your state rules.
rules.roles: Casual babysitting, minor chores around private homes, delivering newspapers to customers.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying.
rules.page_title: Fact Sheet #43: Child Labor Provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for Nonagricultural Occupations

rules.name: Farm and ranch work for teens
rules.age_note: Ages 12 and 13 need written parental consent, unless the farm also employs a parent. Under 12 is allowed only on small farms exempt from federal minimum wage, with parental consent. Children of any age may work on a parent's own farm.
rules.roles: Non-hazardous farm jobs outside school hours at 12 and up. At 16 and up, any farm job at any time.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying. It points to the Wage and Hour Division website and helpline.
rules.page_title: Fact Sheet #40: Overview of Youth Employment (Child Labor) Provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for Agricultural Occupations
rules.quote: Youths 12 and 13 years of age may work outside of school hours

rules.name: Farm jobs for 12 and 13 year olds
rules.age_note: Needs written parental consent, unless the farm also employs a parent. OSHA and state rules also apply, and state law may require a higher wage.
rules.roles: Non-hazardous farm jobs outside school hours.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying. It links to a complaint page and the Young Worker Toolkit.
rules.quote: any non-hazardous job on farms that also employ your parent(s)

rules.name: Farm jobs for kids under 12
rules.age_note: Under 12 may work outside school hours in non-hazardous farm jobs only on small farms exempt from federal minimum wage, with parental consent. Children of any age may work in any job on a farm owned or operated by a parent.
rules.roles: Non-hazardous farm work outside school hours on exempt farms with parental consent. Any job on a parent's own farm.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying.
rules.quote: Children of any age may work at any time in any job on a farm

rules.name: State child labor laws and which rule wins
rules.age_note: The page says that where a state child labor law is more restrictive than the federal law, the state law applies. Check your own state.
rules.roles: Not a job. Explains which age and hour rules apply to you, and the page covers maximum hours and nightwork limits for minors.
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not describe applying.
rules.page_title: Selected State Child Labor Standards Affecting Minors Under 18 in Non-farm Employment as of July 15, 2025

rules.name: Hired farm work (US youth farm rules)
rules.age_note: The OSHA page says a youth 12 or 13 can work on a farm only if a parent has given written permission, only outside school hours, and only in non-hazardous jobs. Youth 14 and 15 can work on any farm only when school is not in session, and only in non-hazardous jobs. Youth under 12 can work on a farm only if the farm is not required to pay the federal minimum wage. Hazardous farm jobs are barred under 16.
rules.roles: Non-hazardous farm work for teens; hazardous farm jobs are barred under 16
rules.how_to_apply: The page does not say. Ask the farm owner directly; this page only lists the rules.
rules.page_title: eTools : Youth in Agriculture - Youth Rights and State/Child Laws | Occupational Safety and Health Administration
rules.quote: only if a parent has given written permission
